\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اقتصاد} (iqtiṣād)}{اقتصاد (iqtiṣād)}]{\ar{اقتصاد} (iqtiṣād) — the economy}

\label{lesson:AR-C383-iqtisad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to protest, then the Arabic for a strike.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اقتصاد}}
\textbf{\ar{اقتصاد}} — \emph{iqtiṣād} — \textquotedblleft{}the economy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يتحسن} \ar{الاقتصاد} \ar{ببطء}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yataḥassanu al-iqtiṣād bi-buṭʾ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The economy is improving slowly.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اقتصاد}} (\emph{iqtiṣād}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-ṣ-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to aim at; to keep to the middle way\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Iqtiṣād} is the Form VIII verbal noun, keeping to the middle way: thrift, and so the economy.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iqtiṣād}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iqtiṣād}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yataḥassanu al-iqtiṣād bi-buṭʾ.} — The economy is improving slowly.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to protest, then the Arabic for a strike, then say \emph{iqtiṣād} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{اقتصاد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The economy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ضريبة} (ḍarība)}{ضريبة (ḍarība)}]{\ar{ضريبة} (ḍarība) — a tax}

\label{lesson:AR-C383-dariba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a strike, then the Arabic for the economy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ضريبة}}
\textbf{\ar{ضريبة}} — \emph{ḍarība} — \textquotedblleft{}a tax\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{دفع} \ar{أبي} \ar{الضريبة} \ar{أمس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dafaʿa abī aḍ-ḍarība ams.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father paid the tax yesterday.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ضريبة}} (\emph{ḍarība}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḍ-r-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to strike, to beat\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A \emph{ḍarība} is what is imposed, struck on someone: a tax.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a strike, then the Arabic for the economy, then say \emph{ḍarība} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عجز} (ʿajz)}{عجز (ʿajz)}]{\ar{عجز} (ʿajz) — a deficit}

\label{lesson:AR-C383-ajz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for the economy, then the Arabic for a tax.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عجز}}
\textbf{\ar{عجز}} — \emph{ʿajz} — \textquotedblleft{}a deficit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{عند} \ar{الدولة} \ar{عجز} \ar{كبير} \ar{هذه} \ar{السنة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ʿinda ad-dawla ʿajz kabīr hādhihi as-sana.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The state has a big deficit this year.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عجز}} (\emph{ʿajz}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-j-z}, \textquotedblleft{}to be unable, weak\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{ʿAjz} is inability, falling short: a deficit.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for giving reasons and opinions.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تضخم} (taḍakhkhum)}{تضخم (taḍakhkhum)}]{\ar{تضخم} (taḍakhkhum) — inflation}

\label{lesson:AR-C383-tadakhkhum}

\end{cousinweb}

One more word for giving reasons and opinions.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استثمر} (istathmara)}{استثمر (istathmara)}]{\ar{استثمر} (istathmara) — to invest}

\label{lesson:AR-C383-istathmara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a deficit, then the Arabic for inflation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استثمر}}
\textbf{\ar{استثمر}} — \emph{istathmara} — \textquotedblleft{}to invest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{استثمر} \ar{عمي} \ar{ماله} \ar{في} \ar{شركة} \ar{صغيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{istathmara ʿammī mālahu fī sharika ṣaghīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My uncle invested his money in a small company.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستثمر}, \emph{yastathmir}.

The noun \ar{استثمار}, \emph{istithmār}, an investment.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استثمر}} (\emph{istathmara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{th-m-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to bear fruit\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form X, to seek fruit from a thing: to invest.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}
